title: What 200,000 Adverse-Event Reports Actually Say About Drugs in Early 2024
subtitle: Reading the FDA's FAERS database as a megaphone, not a measurement
core_claim: FAERS is less a record of what drugs do to people than a record of which drugs the world is paying attention to.
tension: The Ozempic press narrative says one thing; the FAERS 2024 sample says the loudest signal is Mounjaro, and the loudest 'reaction' is not a reaction at all.
payoff: After reading, the reader should know how to read FAERS headlines: as a measure of reporting behaviour first, and only secondarily as a clue to what drugs are actually doing.

edt_01.label: The top complaint isn't medical
edt_01.title: The top complaint isn't medical
edt_01.editorial_notes: 14,801 (Off label use), 11,335 (Drug ineffective), 9,356 (Death as a reaction), 3,554 (Drug-ineffective-only reports) must be exact. The interactive should let the reader scan the top-30 reactions and notice how few of them are medical events.

edt_02.label: What FAERS is, and what its biggest numbers actually mean
edt_02.title: What FAERS is, and what its biggest numbers actually mean
edt_02.editorial_notes: Time-window caveat (Jan 1 – Feb 23) and no-denominator caveat must be visible here. 52.5% (serious), 9.43% (death), 19.06% (hospitalization), 200,000 (sample size) are load-bearing.

edt_03.label: Dupixent and Mounjaro are tied for #1
edt_03.title: Dupixent and Mounjaro are tied for #1
edt_03.editorial_notes: Dupixent 15,027 vs Mounjaro 14,908 — keep the 119-row gap visible. The role-mix point (aspirin 15.8% suspect, acetaminophen 49% suspect) is the key 'don't confuse mention with blame' frame.

edt_04.label: The GLP-1 surge is real, but the spotlight is on the wrong drug
edt_04.title: The GLP-1 surge is real, but the spotlight is on the wrong drug
edt_04.editorial_notes: Tirzepatide 18,035 vs semaglutide 5,425 (ratio 3.3x). Mounjaro 11.0% serious vs Ozempic 32.0% serious. Zepbound 2.5% serious / 0 deaths is the headline outlier. This is THE story — do not undersell.

edt_05.label: Mounjaro's complaints are about the pen; Ozempic's are about the body
edt_05.title: Mounjaro's complaints are about the pen; Ozempic's are about the body
edt_05.editorial_notes: Use the side-by-side reaction lists explicitly. The 'Weight loss poor' AND 'Increased appetite' coexistence is the killer paragraph — it captures the class paradox in two lines.

edt_06.label: The actual death-rate hotspots are nowhere near the headlines
edt_06.title: The actual death-rate hotspots are nowhere near the headlines
edt_06.editorial_notes: Methamphetamine 93.5%, alcohol 89.4%, fentanyl 71.9% — frame as overdose signature, NOT as 'these drugs kill'. Be careful: these are co-presence findings, not causation.

edt_07.label: Who files, when, and from where
edt_07.title: Who files, when, and from where
edt_07.editorial_notes: The weekday/weekend pattern (93% of reports come on weekdays) is the most visceral 'bureaucracy, not events' finding. The map of occurcountry secondary.

edt_08.label: How to read the next FAERS headline
edt_08.title: How to read the next FAERS headline
edt_08.editorial_notes: Repeat the megaphone-not-measurement frame. End on an open question / a directive, not a summary.
